company.name: Harbor Desk
company.one_liner: AI support agent for e-commerce merchants

problem.statement: Small merchants answer the same forty questions every day; support is the first thing that breaks when a store grows.
evidence_given: 'the same forty questions every day' — a specific figure with no source or sample behind it

solution.description: An agent trained on the merchant's own catalogue and policy documents, deployed as a chat widget.
solution.how_it_works: Trained on merchant-supplied catalogue and policy documents; deployed as a chat widget in under ten minutes. No detail beyond that.

business_model.acv_or_arpu: Not stated. Inferring only: $240k ARR across 34 merchants implies roughly $7k per merchant.

competition.positioning_claim: Gorgias and Tidio serve this segment with rule-based flows. We are the only fully agentic option.
competitors_omitted_suspicion: The 'only fully agentic option' claim is exclusive and therefore falsifiable by a single counterexample; no general-purpose support platform is named
Platform-native support tooling from the e-commerce platforms themselves is not mentioned
Large horizontal support vendors that have added AI agents are not mentioned

claims.claim: Customer support software for e-commerce is a $12B market growing 19% a year
Gorgias and Tidio serve this segment with rule-based flows
We are the only fully agentic option
Small merchants answer the same forty questions every day
Deployed as a chat widget in under ten minutes

missing_sections: Retention or churn — absent for a product sold to small merchants, where churn is the defining metric
vague_language: 'the same forty questions every day' — precise-sounding, unsourced
'fully agentic' is used as a category boundary but never defined
deck_quality.notes: The load-bearing claim here is not the market number but the exclusivity claim on slide 5: 'we are the only fully agentic option'. That is the kind of claim that costs a founder credibility if a single counterexample exists, and the competition slide characterizes the two named rivals as rule-based without saying when that was last checked. The market slide gives a size and a growth rate with no methodology and no segment definition, so there is no way to tell whether $12B means e-commerce support specifically or all customer support software. Traction is small but coherent for seed; the missing metric is retention, which for a $7k-ACV product sold to small merchants is the number that decides whether the business exists.
